name: iterm2-control-mcp
description: Open and control interactive iTerm2 terminal sessions — run shell commands, read output, and manage multiple named sessions. Use this when asked to open a terminal, run commands, check system state, or work in a shell.

cleanup_on_close.title: Cleanup on window close
cleanup_on_close.description: Automatically clean up the session when the iTerm2 window is closed

command_markers.title: AI command markers
command_markers.description: Visually highlight AI-sent commands in the terminal with a # [ai] marker line. Makes it easy to distinguish AI commands from user-typed commands.

theme_profile.title: iTerm2 profile name
theme_profile.description: Use an existing iTerm2 profile for session windows. Leave empty for the default orange theme.

max_sessions.title: Max connected sessions
max_sessions.description: Maximum number of sessions that stay connected simultaneously. Oldest inactive session is dropped when the limit is reached.

max_log_mb.title: Max session log size (MB)
max_log_mb.description: Per-session log file is rotated at this size, keeping one backup (total ~2× on disk per session). Set to 0 to disable rotation.

tools.name: iterm_list_sessions
tools.description: List all active terminal sessions with their IDs, names, and status

tools.name: iterm_new_session
tools.description: Open a new iTerm2 terminal window on your LOCAL Mac. The user types directly in the terminal at any time (SSH, docker exec, prompts). Do not speculate about how the terminal reached its state — report what you observe.

tools.name: iterm_connect_session
tools.description: Connect to an existing session by ID or name. Required before sending commands or reading output.

tools.name: iterm_detach_session
tools.description: Detach from the current session. Releases the iTerm2 terminal — the session daemon stays alive and can be reconnected later.

tools.name: iterm_rename_session
tools.description: Rename an active session. Updates metadata and window title.

tools.name: iterm_focus_window
tools.description: Bring the session's iTerm2 window to the front and give it keyboard focus.

tools.name: iterm_split_pane
tools.description: Split the terminal into two panes. Creates a new session for the new pane.

tools.name: iterm_stop_session
tools.description: Stop and destroy a session. Closes the iTerm2 pane by default (and the window if it was the only pane). Pass close_window=false to keep the pane open with a [stopped] title.

tools.name: iterm_clean_sessions
tools.description: Remove stale session directories where the daemon is no longer running

tools.name: iterm_send_command
tools.description: Type and execute a shell command. Use iterm_read_output or iterm_capture_screen to check the result. If no output, command may still be running — check if shell prompt has returned.

tools.name: iterm_send_and_read
tools.description: Send a command and return output in one call. Shared terminal — user types at any time (SSH, docker exec, prompts). When you see commands you didn't send, the user typed them. Report observations, don't speculate.

tools.name: iterm_send_keys
tools.description: Send special keys like Ctrl+C, Ctrl+D, arrows, Tab, Escape for interactive programs

tools.name: iterm_type
tools.description: Type text into the terminal without pressing Enter. Use when the user asks to stage a command for review, pre-fill partial input, or demonstrate without executing.

tools.name: iterm_read_output
tools.description: Read recent terminal output. Shared terminal — buffer contains ALL activity, yours and the user's. Commands you didn't send were typed by the user. Don't speculate about automatic actions. Optionally wait for text or clear buffer.

tools.name: iterm_pipe
tools.description: Forward a chunk of one session's output into another session's pane as if typed. Chain with iterm_send_command's returned cursor to stream a command's output across sessions without a leading-edge race.

tools.name: iterm_capture_screen
tools.description: Snapshot of visible terminal screen with cursor position. Check if shell prompt is on last line (idle) or not (command running). Screen may show user activity — report observations, don't speculate.

tools.name: iterm_probe_environment
tools.description: Get a discovery command sequence to fingerprint the environment. Run commands via iterm_send_and_read.

tools.name: iterm_download_file
tools.description: Download a file from the remote terminal to your Mac via iTerm2 OSC 1337. File is saved to ~/Downloads.

tools.name: iterm_upload_file
tools.description: Write a file to the remote system. Pass local_path for binary files (connector reads from this Mac) or content+encoding for inline payloads.

tools.name: iterm_status
tools.description: Get session info: ID, attached state, uptime, buffer size
